# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

      # consumer here is the pure-python coverage ratchet below — system

      - name: python3 available

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`

That means the "already running" hub and the new hub would BOTH be listening, and incoming WebSocket connections would be randomly routed to either process. # them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only
  # provider-smoke job; perf has its own #303 trajectory gate; browser-ext
  # its own workflow. `pty` marks child-agent-spawn tests whose second
  # process boot is unbounded under runner load (issue #553, red twice on
  # this leg) — they stay in nightly's pty-integration job.
  integration-mock:
    name: Integration tests (mock LLM)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: needs.changes.outputs.intmock == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks before the first test
      # process boots fa (same rationale as the pty-integration leg).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null

      - name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        run: dart test test/integration --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:

---
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # setup-python hardcodes AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY=/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache
      # on every macOS runner (hosted layout assumption) and overwrites
      # RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, so on self-hosted macs without a 'runner' user it
      # dies with "mkdir: /Users/runner: Permission denied". The only python
      # consumer here is the pure-python coverage ratchet below — system
      # python3 (CLT on macOS, preinstalled on hosted images) suffices.
      - name: python3 available
        run: python3 --version
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #943 (vector 3): one warm fa boot before the PTY legs. The
      # first `dart` invocation pays the native-assets build hooks (20-30 s
      # under load) — paid HERE instead of inside a test's boot timeout
      # (tui_prototype_snapshot ×5 on 2026-09-24). Both invocation shapes
      # the tests use (file path + `dart run`) are warmed.
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext)
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage
      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py

DAP_MASTER_SECRET would NOT be inherited (not in whitelist) — so the hub plugin stays disabled unless a test sets DAP_MASTER_SECRET via extraEnv. So the dead-URL pin is defense-in-depth for tests that DO exercise the hub: they pass their own URLs via extraEnv, which overrides. Wait — "Tests that exercise the hub pass their own URLs via [extraEnv] (spread after these)" — spread AFTER means extraEnv wins. ✓ correct order.

So the `DAP_HUB_URL: ws://127.0.0.1:1/ws` default only matters in tests that set DAP_MASTER_SECRET but no explicit URL. A microsecond-refused dial on loopback every N seconds is harmless in tests. Fine.

One consideration: connecting to port 1 — on some systems, connecting to a privileged port that nothing listens on gives ECONNREFUSED instantly. Yes, port 1 on loopback has no listener → RST → instant refuse. Good choice.

The harness comment says the pin prevents "auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub". `resolveDapLocalHubUrl` — the `/dap start` flow probes and spawns. blocks.text:
Confirmed: archive's `lastModTime` is `late int = DateTime.now()...` — the PR's diagnosis is accurate. Pinning to 315532800 (1980-01-01T00:00:00Z) — DOS year field is 7 bits (0-127 added to 1980), month 4 bits, day 5 bits: for 1980-01-01, encoding = (0<<25)|(1<<21)|(1<<16)|... = fine, round-trips.

Wait — check the pin value: 315532800 seconds since Unix epoch = 1980-01-01T00:00:00Z? 315532800 / 86400 = 3652.0 days exactly → 1970 + 3652 days = 1980-01-01. ✓ (10 years with 2 leap days 1972, 1976 = 3652 days). Yes.

Now an interesting subtlety in `serve onto a taken port: bind failure, exit 1` test (pre-existing): the blocker is a plain ServerSocket bound WITHOUT shared → the hub's shared:true bind fails with EADDRINUSE ✓ → hubHealthz on the port → raw socket destroys → returns false → retry → ... 5 attempts → refused → exit 1. This test now takes the FULL retry window: ~2.25s backoff + up to 5 × 1s healthz timeouts... actually each healthz on a destroying socket fails fast (connection accepted then destroyed → the GET may fail fast). So ~2.25s+ runtime, within the 20s timeout. OK but slower.

And "serve against a live hub" — hub answers healthz → exit 0 immediately. ✓

Now — the pre-existing test "serve onto a taken port: bind failure, exit 1" comment says "A non-HTTP listener: connections die instantly, so the healthz probe reports down and the bind is what fails." — with shared:true on LINUX the bind still fails against a non-shared holder ✓. On macOS: Dart's HttpServer.bind shared:true sets SO_REUSEPORT; binding over a socket without SO_REUSEPORT fails ✓. On WINDOWS: shared:true uses SO_REUSEADDR which ALLOWS binding over any existing socket (even non-shared) → this test would FAIL on Windows and the hub would silently hijack the port. The repo tests run on Linux/macOS only (probably). It's a platform-semantics hazard worth one comment line — the hub is cross-platform Dart. Hmm, is it? Let me check if hub serve is supported on Windows... The repo supports Windows for the CLI. But is this a blocking issue? The CI doesn't run hub tests on Windows (no windows jobs seen). Users on Windows could hit silent port hijack... but the hub is a dev tool; the pre-existing "already running" probe still exits 0 against a healthy hub. The hijack scenario on Windows: foreign server on 8787 (non-fa) → hub serve binds over it?? Actually SO_REUSEADDR on Windows: "allows a socket to forcibly bind to a port in use by another socket" — yes, second bind succeeds and behavior is undefined-ish (usually the second socket hijacks). This is a genuine platform-specific correctness concern → IMPORTANT (not blocking since CI platforms are POSIX and it matches Dart's documented cross-platform caveat... actually it IS a real behavior regression on Windows).

Wait, I should double check Dart's HttpServer.bind documentation:
```
/// If [shared] is `true` ... multiple [HttpServer]s can bind to the same port...
/// The default is `false`.
```
Dart SDK docs for ServerSocket.bind:
```
/// If [shared] is `true`, the socket is bound with `SO_REUSEPORT` on POSIX...
/// On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` is used, which allows the socket to bind even if
/// another socket has it bound... 
```
Actually the exact Dart doc: "If shared is true and the port is already bound by another socket, the socket binds successfully... on Linux/MacOS SO_REUSEPORT; on Windows SO_REUSEADDR". Yes — Windows SO_REUSEADDR semantics allow hijacking. Confirmed hazard.

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

With `shared: true` on Linux, two sockets can bind the same port with SO_REUSEPORT... wait, Dart's `shared: true` sets SO_REUSEPORT on Linux and SO_REUSEADDR on Windows/macOS? Let me think. Before this PR: EADDRINUSE → exit 1 (clear failure). Now: silent split-brain. Probability: hub wedged-but-listening is rare (the event loop must be alive to accept, but slow). Healthz timeout is 1s, so a heavily loaded machine could delay the healthz response >1s while the hub is alive and accepting connections → new bind succeeds → two live hubs sharing the port → connections randomly split between two independent hub processes with independent state (pid file overwritten by the new one, sessions enrolled one not visible to the other). The env whitelist: TERM/LANG/LOGNAME/USER/DISPLAY/LC_TYPE/HOME/PATH + PUB_CACHE + DAP_HUB_URL/DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL + extraEnv. DAP_MASTER_SECRET would NOT be inherited (not in whitelist) — so the hub plugin stays disabled unless a test sets DAP_MASTER_SECRET via extraEnv. So the dead-URL pin is defense-in-depth for tests that DO exercise the hub: they pass their own URLs via extraEnv, which overrides. Wait — "Tests that exercise the hub pass their own URLs via [extraEnv] (spread after these)" — spread AFTER means extraEnv wins. ✓ correct order.

So the `DAP_HUB_URL: ws://127.0.0.1:1/ws` default only matters in tests that set DAP_MASTER_SECRET but no explicit URL. Then the CLI dials port 1 → refused instantly → "[hub] connect failed: ..." printed once. Does HubClient retry forever in background? Let me check quickly for reconnect logic. Actually the kill-switch comment says "no connection, no reconnect" for the disabled case. For the enabled-but-dead case, there may be a reconnect loop. A microsecond-refused dial on loopback every N seconds is harmless in tests. Fine.

One consideration: connecting to port 1 — on some systems, connecting to a privileged port that nothing listens on gives ECONNREFUSED instantly. Yes, port 1 on loopback has no listener → RST → instant refuse. Good choice.

Now, is there anywhere in the CLI that AUTO-STARTS the hub when DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL is set but unhealthy? The harness comment says the pin prevents "auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub". `resolveDapLocalHubUrl` — the `/dap start` flow probes and spawns. Confirmed: archive's `lastModTime` is `late int = DateTime.now()...` — the PR's diagnosis is accurate. Pinning to 315532800 (1980-01-01T00:00:00Z) — DOS year field is 7 bits (0-127 added to 1980), month 4 bits, day 5 bits: for 1980-01-01, encoding = (0<<25)|(1<<21)|(1<<16)|... = fine, round-trips.

Wait — check the pin value: 315532800 seconds since Unix epoch = 1980-01-01T00:00:00Z? 315532800 / 86400 = 3652.0 days exactly → 1970 + 3652 days = 1980-01-01. ✓ (10 years with 2 leap days 1972, 1976 = 3652 days). Yes.

Now an interesting subtlety in `serve onto a taken port: bind failure, exit 1` test (pre-existing): the blocker is a plain ServerSocket bound WITHOUT shared → the hub's shared:true bind fails with EADDRINUSE ✓ → hubHealthz on the port → raw socket destroys → returns false → retry → ... 5 attempts → refused → exit 1. This test now takes the FULL retry window: ~2.25s backoff + up to 5 × 1s healthz timeouts... actually each healthz on a destroying socket fails fast (connection accepted then destroyed → the GET may fail fast). So ~2.25s+ runtime, within the 20s timeout. OK but slower.

And "serve against a live hub" — hub answers healthz → exit 0 immediately. ✓

Now — the pre-existing test "serve onto a taken port: bind failure, exit 1" comment says "A non-HTTP listener: connections die instantly, so the healthz probe reports down and the bind is what fails." — with shared:true on LINUX the bind still fails against a non-shared holder ✓. On macOS: Dart's HttpServer.bind shared:true sets SO_REUSEPORT; binding over a socket without SO_REUSEPORT fails ✓. On WINDOWS: shared:true uses SO_REUSEADDR which ALLOWS binding over any existing socket (even non-shared) → this test would FAIL on Windows and the hub would silently hijack the port. The repo tests run on Linux/macOS only (probably). It's a platform-semantics hazard worth one comment line — the hub is cross-platform Dart. Hmm, is it? Let me check if hub serve is supported on Windows... The repo supports Windows for the CLI. But is this a blocking issue? The CI doesn't run hub tests on Windows (no windows jobs seen). Users on Windows could hit silent port hijack... but the hub is a dev tool; the pre-existing "already running" probe still exits 0 against a healthy hub. The hijack scenario on Windows: foreign server on 8787 (non-fa) → hub serve binds over it?? Actually SO_REUSEADDR on Windows: "allows a socket to forcibly bind to a port in use by another socket" — yes, second bind succeeds and behavior is undefined-ish (usually the second socket hijacks). This is a genuine platform-specific correctness concern → IMPORTANT (not blocking since CI platforms are POSIX and it matches Dart's documented cross-platform caveat... actually it IS a real behavior regression on Windows).

Wait, I should double check Dart's HttpServer.bind documentation:
```
/// If [shared] is `true` ... multiple [HttpServer]s can bind to the same port...
/// The default is `false`.
```
Dart SDK docs for ServerSocket.bind:
```
/// If [shared] is `true`, the socket is bound with `SO_REUSEPORT` on POSIX...
/// On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` is used, which allows the socket to bind even if
/// another socket has it bound... 
```
Actually the exact Dart doc: "If shared is true and the port is already bound by another socket, the socket binds successfully... on Linux/MacOS SO_REUSEPORT; on Windows SO_REUSEADDR". Yes — Windows SO_REUSEADDR semantics allow hijacking. Confirmed hazard.

re-read changed files,

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

1. **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — 3x duplicated prewarm steps. Check: secrets, pinning (uses actions/upload-artifact@SHA — pre-existing), permissions. The prewarm steps duplicate the same 5 lines 3 times — potential duplication finding (SUGGESTION: could use a composite action, but that's arguably overkill; duplication in YAML workflow steps is common). Also check: does `dart bin/fah.dart --help` require `dart pub get` first? In the first hunk (line ~404), the prewarm step is inserted after a cache restore step. Need to check if `dart pub get` runs before it in each job. If pub get hasn't run, `dart bin/fah.dart --help` would fail (missing package_config). Let me examine ci.yml around those lines.

2. **`bin/fah_hub_serve.dart`** — the bind retry logic:
   - `_bindBackoff(attempt)` — `150 << (attempt - 1)` for attempt 1..4 gives 150,300,600,1200; the 5th attempt never delays since `_bindAttempt` with lastAttempt returns refused/retry... Actually wait: on attempt 5, if outcome == retry... `_bindAttempt(hub, port, lastAttempt: true)`: on SocketException with lastAttempt → refused. So retry can't be returned on the last attempt. But what if `hub.start()` throws something OTHER than SocketException? Then it propagates — fine (unchanged behavior... actually the old code also only caught SocketException).
   - **Important correctness issue**: `shared: true` changes the semantics of binding. With `shared: true` on Linux, two sockets can bind the same port with SO_REUSEPORT... wait, Dart's `shared: true` sets SO_REUSEPORT on Linux and SO_REUSEADDR on Windows/macOS? Let me think. Dart `HttpServer.bind({bool shared = false})`: "When shared is set to true, the socket is bound with SO_REUSEPORT so multiple isolates/processes can bind to the same port" — actually on Dart, `shared: true` uses `SO_REUSEPORT` on Linux and macOS? The docs: "If shared is true and the port is already bound, the socket is bound with the SO_REUSEPORT flag" — hmm, actually Dart's documentation says: "When shared is true, the socket sets SO_REUSEPORT before binding, which allows multiple sockets to bind to the same address/port... On Windows, SO_REUSEADDR is used". 

   The KEY security/correctness concern: with `shared: true`, a bind to a port already held by a NON-shared socket still fails with EADDRINUSE. That's what the test relies on ("a foreign NON-shared holder still fails the bind"). And two shared sockets CAN bind simultaneously — meaning two hub processes serve the same port, with the kernel load-balancing connections between them! On Linux, SO_REUSEPORT distributes incoming connections across all sockets bound to the same port. That means the "already running" hub and the new hub would BOTH be listening, and incoming WebSocket connections would be randomly routed to either process. That is a real correctness hazard: the retry path's `hubHealthz` probe mitigates it (if a live hub answers /healthz, we exit 0), but there's a race window: if the predecessor hub is dying/slow and doesn't answer healthz but still holds the shared socket open... Actually with shared:true both binds succeed, and the healthz probe could hit EITHER socket — the kernel load-balances. Hmm, but the probe only happens after a failed bind attempt. Sequence: attempt 1 bind fails (predecessor holds port non-shared? no — predecessor bound shared:true now!).

Hub B proceeds to serve alongside hub A! The kernel load-balances new connections between A and B. The idempotency probe (hubServe checks /healthz BEFORE trying to bind? Let me check the code) — the old comment says "idempotent against a live one" — `hubServe` probes /healthz first, and takes the "already running" exit if live. So a healthy predecessor is detected by the probe before bind. The bind retry only kicks in when the probe fails (predecessor dying/dead but port still held). In that window with shared:true:
   - If predecessor is in the middle of shutting down (socket closed), port might be in TIME_WAIT... shared bind succeeds, fine, hub B serves. OK.
   - If predecessor is STILL LISTENING but unresponsive (wedged, not answering /healthz within probe timeout): hub B binds shared:true successfully → BOTH listen → kernel load-balances future connections → connections randomly land on the wedged A or the healthy B. This is a genuine hazard introduced by shared:true: the hub on this port becomes nondeterministically split. Before the PR, bind would fail with EADDRINUSE → exit 1 → clear failure. Now: silent split-brain.

   Hmm, but on Linux, SO_REUSEPORT requires ALL sockets binding the same port to set SO_REUSEPORT (bind fails with EADDRINUSE if the existing socket didn't set it). Dart's `shared: true` sets SO_REUSEPORT... on which platforms? Dart docs for HttpServer.bind: "If shared is set to true... the socket is bound with SO_REUSEPORT" — I believe this applies to Linux and macOS (macOS supports SO_REUSEPORT too, though semantics differ: on macOS SO_REUSEPORT allows multiple binds but WITHOUT load balancing — only the last bound socket receives? Actually on macOS, SO_REUSEPORT allows multiple binds and connections go to the most recent socket... it varies). On Windows, `shared: true` uses SO_REUSEADDR which allows hijacking ANY bound port — even a non-shared one! That's a known Dart issue: on Windows, shared:true + SO_REUSEADDR can steal a port from a non-shared holder. But the CI runs on Linux/macOS runners; the harness targets dev machines. On Windows fa users... the hub serve on Windows with shared:true could bind over a foreign holder without EADDRINUSE. Hmm, this is a potential correctness/security concern but platform-specific.

   The local_hub_test change pins the new contract: "binding a TAKEN port shares it" — the second LocalHub.start() SUCCEEDS while the first is live, both serving. The test even asserts `second.url.port == first.url.port` and first keeps serving after second stops. So at the LocalHub layer, a taken port NO LONGER throws. The idempotency now rests entirely on hubServe's /healthz pre-probe. What about other LocalHub.start() callers? Let me grep for `LocalHub(` and `.start()` callers in lib/ and bin/. Need to grep callers.

Key observations so far:

1. `hubHealthz` has `connectionTimeout = 1s` and catches everything → bounded. Good. Total retry window: 5 attempts × (bind fail + healthz ≤1s) + backoffs 150+300+600+1200 = 2250ms + up to ~5s healthz = bounded ~7-8s. OK.

2. **The split-brain concern**: `hubServe` probes /healthz first. If a live hub answers → exit 0 (no bind). Only when the probe fails do we try to bind — now with `shared: true`. Scenarios:
   - Predecessor fully dead, port in TIME_WAIT → shared bind succeeds → serve. ✓ (this is the fix's purpose)
   - Predecessor still listening (shared:true) but wedged/not answering healthz within 1s → bind SUCCEEDS (both shared) → both hubs listen on the port → kernel load-balances new connections between a wedged hub and a fresh hub. Before this PR: EADDRINUSE → exit 1 (clear failure). Now: silent split-brain. Probability: hub wedged-but-listening is rare (the event loop must be alive to accept, but slow). Healthz timeout is 1s, so a heavily loaded machine could delay the healthz response >1s while the hub is alive and accepting connections → new bind succeeds → two live hubs sharing the port → connections randomly split between two independent hub processes with independent state (pid file overwritten by the new one, sessions enrolled one not visible to the other). This is a REAL behavioral hazard introduced by shared:true at the LocalHub layer. Severity: IMPORTANT (not blocking — the hub is a local dev tool; window is narrow; hubServe probes first; but the failure mode changed from loud exit-1 to silent connection splitting).

   Wait, actually — on Linux, when two sockets listen with SO_REUSEPORT on the same port, incoming connections are distributed (hash by 4-tuple). Both hubs answer /healthz with 200. `fa dap stop` reads pid file → SIGTERMs the newest pid → one hub dies, the other keeps the port. The roster/sessions are split. Yes — silent corruption.

   Also on Windows: Dart maps `shared: true` to SO_REUSEADDR — which on Windows allows binding over a NON-shared socket too (SO_REUSEADDR on Windows ≈ SO_REUSEADDR|SO_REUSEPORT semantics — it can hijack). So a genuinely foreign holder on Windows would be bound-over instead of exit-1. The PR's test "foreign NON-shared holder still fails the bind" runs on Linux/macOS CI. Platform divergence — worth a note.

   Hmm, but wait — actually let me double-check Dart's semantics for `shared: true` on Linux: it sets SO_REUSEPORT. If the EXISTING socket was bound WITHOUT SO_REUSEPORT (e.g., a foreign server), the new bind fails with EADDRINUSE. ✓ matches the test contract. If the existing socket HAS SO_REUSEPORT (another fa hub), bind succeeds → split brain. The healthz pre-probe mitigates the healthy case; only the wedged case slips through.

   And there's a second race: TWO `fa hub serve` starting SIMULTANEOUSLY (overlapping CI runs booting at the same moment): both probe healthz → both fail → both bind shared:true → both succeed → both write pid file → split brain from the start. No retry window saves you here since bind SUCCEEDS. Before the PR: one wins, other exits 1. This is a genuine regression in mutual exclusion. The "already running" idempotency now depends on a healthz race. IMPORTANT.

   Mitigating factor: in the CI scenario the PR targets, the port is the zero-config 8787? Actually tests pin DAP_HUB_URL to port 1, and hub tests use explicit ports. The hub serve with a taken port mid-retry — the target scenario is "predecessor dying". The simultaneous-boot scenario is exactly what overlapping CI runs do... but each run uses its own port? `fa hub serve` default port is 8787 (zero-config). Two overlapping CI runs both running `fa dap start`/hub serve on default 8787 → simultaneous → split brain. Hmm, but tests now pin DAP_HUB_URL to port 1 so tests never auto-start hubs... The PTY tests that exercise the hub pass their own URLs. So in the CI context the vector is reduced. Still worth flagging as IMPORTANT with suggested mitigation (e.g., post-bind re-probe: after a shared bind, check that we're the only listener — can't easily; or use a pid-file/advisory lock (flock) for mutual exclusion; or keep bind non-shared and only retry on EADDRINUSE — the retry alone without shared:true would handle the dying-predecessor case!).

   Actually that's the key insight: **the retry alone (without shared:true) covers the stated scenario**. A dying predecessor eventually releases the port (socket closed → EADDRINUSE stops) → attempt N binds. TIME_WAIT doesn't hold a LISTEN socket — a closed listening socket leaves no TIME_WAIT for incoming binds with SO_REUSEADDR (Dart sets SO_REUSEADDR by default? HttpServer.bind sets... Dart's ServerSocket.bind has shared param; without shared, on Linux it sets SO_REUSEADDR which ignores TIME_WAIT). So retry-without-shared would pick up the dying predecessor's port within the backoff window. shared:true ADDS only the coexistence hazard. I should flag: consider dropping shared:true; the healthz-aware retry suffices for the "dying predecessor" vector. But the PR deliberately changed the local_hub contract test to pin sharing behavior ("binding a TAKEN port shares it"). It's a design decision worth challenging in review → IMPORTANT.

3. **hubServe probe + bind for LAN bind**: hubLanSecretRefusal check happens AFTER the initial healthz probe but BEFORE bind — unchanged ordering. OK.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: archive's `lastModTime` is `late int = DateTime.now()...` — the PR's diagnosis is accurate. Pinning to 315532800 (1980-01-01T00:00:00Z) — DOS year field is 7 bits (0-127 added to 1980), month 4 bits, day 5 bits: for 1980-01-01, encoding = (0<<25)|(1<<21)|(1<<16)|... = fine, round-trips.

Wait — check the pin value: 315532800 seconds since Unix epoch = 1980-01-01T00:00:00Z? 315532800 / 86400 = 3652.0 days exactly → 1970 + 3652 days = 1980-01-01. ✓ (10 years with 2 leap days 1972, 1976 = 3652 days). Yes.

Now an interesting subtlety in `serve onto a taken port: bind failure, exit 1` test (pre-existing): the blocker is a plain ServerSocket bound WITHOUT shared → the hub's shared:true bind fails with EADDRINUSE ✓ → hubHealthz on the port → raw socket destroys → returns false → retry → ... 5 attempts → refused → exit 1. This test now takes the FULL retry window: ~2.25s backoff + up to 5 × 1s healthz timeouts... actually each healthz on a destroying socket fails fast (connection accepted then destroyed → the GET may fail fast). So ~2.25s+ runtime, within the 20s timeout. OK but slower.

And "serve against a live hub" — hub answers healthz → exit 0 immediately. ✓

Now — the pre-existing test "serve onto a taken port: bind failure, exit 1" comment says "A non-HTTP listener: connections die instantly, so the healthz probe reports down and the bind is what fails." — with shared:true on LINUX the bind still fails against a non-shared holder ✓. On macOS: Dart's HttpServer.bind shared:true sets SO_REUSEPORT; binding over a socket without SO_REUSEPORT fails ✓. On WINDOWS: shared:true uses SO_REUSEADDR which ALLOWS binding over any existing socket (even non-shared) → this test would FAIL on Windows and the hub would silently hijack the port. The repo tests run on Linux/macOS only (probably). It's a platform-semantics hazard worth one comment line — the hub is cross-platform Dart. Hmm, is it? Let me check if hub serve is supported on Windows... The repo supports Windows for the CLI. But is this a blocking issue? The CI doesn't run hub tests on Windows (no windows jobs seen). Users on Windows could hit silent port hijack... but the hub is a dev tool; the pre-existing "already running" probe still exits 0 against a healthy hub. The hijack scenario on Windows: foreign server on 8787 (non-fa) → hub serve binds over it?? Actually SO_REUSEADDR on Windows: "allows a socket to forcibly bind to a port in use by another socket" — yes, second bind succeeds and behavior is undefined-ish (usually the second socket hijacks). This is a genuine platform-specific correctness concern → IMPORTANT (not blocking since CI platforms are POSIX and it matches Dart's documented cross-platform caveat... actually it IS a real behavior regression on Windows).

Wait, I should double check Dart's HttpServer.bind documentation:
```
/// If [shared] is `true` ... multiple [HttpServer]s can bind to the same port...
/// The default is `false`.
```
Dart SDK docs for ServerSocket.bind:
```
/// If [shared] is `true`, the socket is bound with `SO_REUSEPORT` on POSIX...
/// On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` is used, which allows the socket to bind even if
/// another socket has it bound... 
```
Actually the exact Dart doc: "If shared is true and the port is already bound by another socket, the socket binds successfully... on Linux/MacOS SO_REUSEPORT; on Windows SO_REUSEADDR". Yes — Windows SO_REUSEADDR semantics allow hijacking. Confirmed hazard.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
