# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte

# them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only
  # provider-smoke job; perf has its own #303 trajectory gate; browser-ext
  # its own workflow. `pty` marks child-agent-spawn tests whose second
  # process boot is unbounded under runner load (issue #553, red twice on
  # this leg) — they stay in nightly's pty-integration job.
  integration-mock:
    name: Integration tests (mock LLM)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: needs.changes.outputs.intmock == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks before the first test
      # process boots fa (same rationale as the pty-integration leg).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null

      - name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        run: dart test test/integration --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.

  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

Confirmed: `LocalHub.start()` silently coexists now. The split-brain scenario:

1. **Two simultaneous `fa hub serve` on the same port** (e.g., two overlapping CI runs, or a user double-start racing): both `/healthz` probes fail (neither is up yet), both bind `shared: true` → BOTH succeed → two independent hub processes serving the same port, kernel load-balancing WebSocket connections between them. Peers enrolled on hub A are invisible to hub B; `fa dap stop` SIGTERMs only the pid in the state file (the last writer). Before the PR: the loser exited 1 loudly. **This is a real regression in the idempotency guarantee.**

2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor**: healthz probe times out (1s) under load, bind shared:true succeeds → coexistence with a live-but-slow hub.

The healthz-then-bind window is inherent (TOCTOU), and `shared: true` converts that TOCTOU from "loud exit 1" to "silent split brain". The retry-with-backoff alone (keeping the bind exclusive) would deliver the same "dying predecessor picked up" benefit: a dying hub closes its listening socket, releasing the port; TIME_WAIT doesn't block a fresh listener with default SO_REUSEADDR semantics (Dart sets SO_REUSEADDR on non-shared binds on POSIX).

Hmm wait — actually, is that true? When a LISTENING socket is closed, are there lingering TIME_WAIT sockets that block a new bind? A listening socket with no connections: closing it leaves no TIME_WAIT (TIME_WAIT applies to connections in that state; a socket that only listened never established connections so no TIME_WAIT). If it HAD established connections, those connections' TIME_WAIT could block... with SO_REUSEADDR (which Dart sets by default for non-shared binds on POSIX? Actually Dart's ServerSocket.bind with shared=false sets SO_REUSEADDR on POSIX — yes, Dart always sets SO_REUSEADDR on POSIX binds; `shared: true` ADDS SO_REUSEPORT). So retry-without-shared would succeed once the predecessor's listening socket closes even with lingering TIME_WAIT connections. So shared:true is not strictly needed for the stated vector — the retry alone covers it. shared:true's only added capability: coexistence with a STILL-LISTENING hub — which is exactly the split-brain case. Strong argument: drop shared:true, keep the retry. This is my top finding — IMPORTANT (I'd argue even BLOCKING-adjacent; but let me weigh severity: who runs two hubs on the same port simultaneously? In CI: tests pin DAP_HUB_URL to port 1 and hub tests use ephemeral ports; the zero-config 8787 default port is used by real users' `fa dap start`. Two `fa hub serve` racing on 8787: previously the second exited 1 ("something else holds the port") — hmm, actually previously against a LIVE hub the healthz probe exits 0 first ("already running"). The bind-race only hit when both started within the same second: probe fails on both, then one binds, other gets EADDRINUSE → exit 1 → the `fa dap start` spawner (detached) leaves the hub dead; the CLI then... hmm. With the PR: both bind → both serve → BOTH print "DAP hub on ws://..." → each run's CLI enrolls against whichever hub answers → split roster. For a local dev tool the practical frequency is low but the failure mode is nasty and silent. I'll rate it IMPORTANT with a strong recommendation. Actually, let me reconsider BLOCKING: "merge would cause a bug" — the bug pre-exists as a race; the PR widens the failure mode from loud to silent. The PR's primary goal is fixing flaky infra tests; this change serves vector 2. The tests still pass. It's a design trade-off the author made consciously (documented in local_hub_test). Per severity rules: "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed." The split-brain IS a potential bug introduced... but narrow. When in doubt start one level higher → BLOCKING? Hmm. The merge would introduce silent connection-splitting behavior on a race path that previously failed loudly. I think IMPORTANT is defensible, but the guideline says "When in doubt, start one level higher". The simultaneous-start race is real (overlapping CI runs are exactly the PR's motivating scenario!). In the overlap scenario with default port 8787 and two runs booting hubs simultaneously → split brain. But wait — do the CI PTY runs actually spawn hubs on the same port? After this PR, tests pin DAP_HUB_URL to port 1 and never auto-start the zero-config hub, and hub-exercising tests use their own ports (`--port` from freePort or explicit). The overlap scenario the PR describes ("an overlapping run's predecessor may still hold the port") involves the same port — meaning tests DO share hub ports across runs somewhere (e.g., the composer_tui_grid / picker tests that were skipped for "hub port race"). Let me check what ports those suites use — if two runs pick the same port via freePort() collisions or a fixed port, the simultaneous-bind race applies. Let me look at composer_tui_grid_pty_test and picker_filter_rows_pty_test quickly.

Also Windows SO_REUSEADDR hijack — same finding umbrella.

Let me check the hub port usage in those two suites.

Those suites don't spawn hubs themselves — they were dying because the spawned `fa` CLI auto-dialed the zero-config 8787 hub on the shared runner (another run's orphaned hub). The harness pin (DAP_HUB_URL=port 1) fixes that vector. The shared:true + retry helps the hub-serving suites (fah_hub_serve_ports tests, job_board pty? job_board uses ext processes...).

OK. Now let me also verify the `_bindWithRetry` behavior against a LIVE healthy hub — hubServe pre-probes, exits 0 — retry never runs. ✓. Against a foreign NON-shared holder: bind fails (POSIX), healthz fails → 5 attempts over ~2.25s+ → exit 1 ✓ (slower but bounded, ~2.3-7s).

Now let me examine remaining diff hunks I haven't fully reviewed:
- test/integration/fa_cube_integration_test.dart tearDown ✓ (seen in diff; failure-safe delete; catches FileSystemException — note PathNotFoundException IS a FileSystemException subclass ✓)
- pty_resume_equivalence_test.dart — 90s wait vs 60s budget ✓ logic sound. Test-level @Timeout(Duration(minutes:10)) covers.
- job_board setUp uses createTempSync — two dirs, failure-safe tearDown ✓. One nuance: `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync` in setUp — if the process dies, /tmp residue accumulates (accepted trade-off, documented).
- tui_protype_snapshot_test — default wait 20→60s. Check the file-level @Timeout: the file has `@Tags(['integration'])` — is there a @Timeout? Let me check it doesn't conflict.
- scheduled_indicator_test — only the @Skip removal.
- dap_cli_e2e_test — only @Skip removal.
- ci.yml — checked.

One more check on `_bindBackoff`: `150 << (attempt - 1)` — attempt is 1-based; on attempt 5 the delay would be 2400ms but it's never reached (lastAttempt returns refused). Fine. Comment says 150,300,600,1200 ✓.

`_bindAttempt` returns `(alreadyRunning, error)` — the error is carried but unused by the caller for alreadyRunning (message only printed for refused). Fine.

Exhaustiveness switch: `_BindOutcome.retry: break; // unreachable` ✓.

Now — a subtle one in hubServe: the initial `hubHealthz(spec.port)` probe is hardcoded to 127.0.0.1 — for `bind == 'lan'` the hub binds 0.0.0.0; probing 127.0.0.1 still works. Pre-existing. Fine.

Another subtle issue: `hubServe`'s healthz pre-probe + `_bindWithRetry` — the retry's `hubHealthz(port)` — if the port is held by a FOREIGN HTTP server that answers 200 on /healthz (e.g., some other app!), the hub exits 0 "already running" without serving — a false-positive idempotent no-op. Pre-existing behavior (the initial probe already did this). Not new.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

1. **Two simultaneous `fa hub serve` on the same port** (e.g., two overlapping CI runs, or a user double-start racing): both `/healthz` probes fail (neither is up yet), both bind `shared: true` → BOTH succeed → two independent hub processes serving the same port, kernel load-balancing WebSocket connections between them. Peers enrolled on hub A are invisible to hub B; `fa dap stop` SIGTERMs only the pid in the state file (the last writer). Before the PR: the loser exited 1 loudly. **This is a real regression in the idempotency guarantee.**

2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor**: healthz probe times out (1s) under load, bind shared:true succeeds → coexistence with a live-but-slow hub.

The healthz-then-bind window is inherent (TOCTOU), and `shared: true` converts that TOCTOU from "loud exit 1" to "silent split brain". The retry-with-backoff alone (keeping the bind exclusive) would deliver the same "dying predecessor picked up" benefit: a dying hub closes its listening socket, releasing the port; TIME_WAIT doesn't block a fresh listener with default SO_REUSEADDR semantics (Dart sets SO_REUSEADDR on non-shared binds on POSIX).

Hmm wait — actually, is that true? When a LISTENING socket is closed, are there lingering TIME_WAIT sockets that block a new bind? A listening socket with no connections: closing it leaves no TIME_WAIT (TIME_WAIT applies to connections in that state; a socket that only listened never established connections so no TIME_WAIT). If it HAD established connections, those connections' TIME_WAIT could block... with SO_REUSEADDR (which Dart sets by default for non-shared binds on POSIX? Actually Dart's ServerSocket.bind with shared=false sets SO_REUSEADDR on POSIX — yes, Dart always sets SO_REUSEADDR on POSIX binds; `shared: true` ADDS SO_REUSEPORT). So retry-without-shared would succeed once the predecessor's listening socket closes even with lingering TIME_WAIT connections. So shared:true is not strictly needed for the stated vector — the retry alone covers it. shared:true's only added capability: coexistence with a STILL-LISTENING hub — which is exactly the split-brain case. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# pr-948: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled

## Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed

# them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only
  # provider-smoke job; perf has its own #303 trajectory gate; browser-ext
  # its own workflow. `pty` marks child-agent-spawn tests whose second
  # process boot is unbounded under runner load (issue #553, red twice on
  # this leg) — they stay in nightly's pty-integration job.
  integration-mock:
    name: Integration tests (mock LLM)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: needs.changes.outputs.intmock == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks before the first test
      # process boots fa (same rationale as the pty-integration leg).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null

      - name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        run: dart test test/integration --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

Confirmed: `LocalHub.start()` silently coexists now. The split-brain scenario:

1. **Two simultaneous `fa hub serve` on the same port** (e.g., two overlapping CI runs, or a user double-start racing): both `/healthz` probes fail (neither is up yet), both bind `shared: true` → BOTH succeed → two independent hub processes serving the same port, kernel load-balancing WebSocket connections between them. Before the PR: the loser exited 1 loudly. **This is a real regression in the idempotency guarantee.**

2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor**: healthz probe times out (1s) under load, bind shared:true succeeds → coexistence with a live-but-slow hub.

The healthz-then-bind window is inherent (TOCTOU), and `shared: true` converts that TOCTOU from "loud exit 1" to "silent split brain". The retry-with-backoff alone (keeping the bind exclusive) would deliver the same "dying predecessor picked up" benefit: a dying hub closes its listening socket, releasing the port; TIME_WAIT doesn't block a fresh listener with default SO_REUSEADDR semantics (Dart sets SO_REUSEADDR on non-shared binds on POSIX).

Hmm wait — actually, is that true? When a LISTENING socket is closed, are there lingering TIME_WAIT sockets that block a new bind? Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
