# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte

Confirmed: `LocalHub.start()` silently coexists now. The split-brain scenario:

1. **Two simultaneous `fa hub serve` on the same port** (e.g., two overlapping CI runs, or a user double-start racing): both `/healthz` probes fail (neither is up yet), both bind `shared: true` → BOTH succeed → two independent hub processes serving the same port, kernel load-balancing WebSocket connections between them. Peers enrolled on hub A are invisible to hub B; `fa dap stop` SIGTERMs only the pid in the state file (the last writer). Before the PR: the loser exited 1 loudly. **This is a real regression in the idempotency guarantee.**

2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor**: healthz probe times out (1s) under load, bind shared:true succeeds → coexistence with a live-but-slow hub.

The healthz-then-bind window is inherent (TOCTOU), and `shared: true` converts that TOCTOU from "loud exit 1" to "silent split brain". The retry-with-backoff alone (keeping the bind exclusive) would deliver the same "dying predecessor picked up" benefit: a dying hub closes its listening socket, releasing the port; TIME_WAIT doesn't block a fresh listener with default SO_REUSEADDR semantics (Dart sets SO_REUSEADDR on non-shared binds on POSIX).

Hmm wait — actually, is that true? When a LISTENING socket is closed, are there lingering TIME_WAIT sockets that block a new bind? A listening socket with no connections: closing it leaves no TIME_WAIT (TIME_WAIT applies to connections in that state; a socket that only listened never established connections so no TIME_WAIT). {"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: `shared: true` turns a loud bind failure into a silent split-brain (and silently changes a public API contract)**

`LocalHub.start()` now binds with `shared: true`. On POSIX that sets `SO_REUSEPORT`, so **two fa hubs can bind the same port at the same time and the kernel load-balances new connections between them**. The `/healthz` pre-probe in `hubServe` only covers the "predecessor is already healthy" case; it does not cover:

1. **Simultaneous start** — the exact overlapping-run scenario this PR targets. Both processes fail the pre-probe (neither is up yet), both `shared: true` binds **succeed**, and both hubs serve one port: split roster/enrollments, last-writer-wins pid file, and each client randomly lands on either hub. Before this PR the loser exited 1 loudly ("something else holds the port").
2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor** — probe times out after 1 s under load while the old hub is alive → coexistence instead of a clear failure.
3. **Windows** — Dart maps `shared: true` to `SO_REUSEADDR` there, which binds over *any* existing holder (even a non-shared foreign server). The "foreign holder still exits 1" contract pinned in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` silently breaks on Windows (the CI matrix just doesn't run it there).

Note that the retry alone — without `shared: true` — already covers the stated vector: a dying predecessor's LISTEN socket closes and releases the port, and dart:io sets `SO_REUSEADDR` by default on POSIX, so TIME_WAIT does not block the re-bind. `shared: true` adds *only* the coexistence hazard.

This is also a **public API semantic change**: `LocalHub` is exported from `lib/io.dart`, and `start()` no longer throws `SocketException` on a taken port — that contract change is documented only in a test comment, not on `start()` itself.

Suggested hardening (any one):
- Drop `shared: true`; keep the healthz-aware retry (covers the dying-predecessor case with no split-brain window), or
- Keep it but add a post-bind re-probe: after a successful bind, re-probe `/healthz` for a short window and if *another* hub answers, `stop()` + take the idempotent "already running" exit, and
- Document the new "a second `start()` on a taken port shares it" contract in `start()`'s doc comment.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the 60 s `waitFor` default can never fire — the framework's 30 s per-test timeout binds first**

This file has **no `@Timeout`** (every other PTY suite touched by this PR carries one, e.g. `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))`), `dart_test.yaml` sets no timeout override, and the CI invocation (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext`) passes no `--timeout`. So package:test's **default 30 s per-test timeout** applies.

Consequences for the new 60 s default:

- If the first frame arrives between 30 s and 60 s (the upper half of the stated 20-30 s cold-hook cost, plus margin), the **framework kills the test at 30 s** with a bare "Test timed out after 0:00:30.0" — the raised budget never helps, and the friendly `TimeoutException('pattern not found: … output:\n…')` dump at 60 s is unreachable, so failure diagnostics get *worse* than the old 20 s line.
- The 60 s timer only matters for pattern-not-found runs where the test would already have been torn down.

Fix: add a file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` (or per-test `timeout:`), matching the convention of the other suites in this PR, so the 60 s wait — and its diagnostic — can actually bind.
"}

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: `shared: true` turns a loud bind failure into a silent split-brain (and silently changes a public API contract)**

`LocalHub.start()` now binds with `shared: true`. On POSIX that sets `SO_REUSEPORT`, so **two fa hubs can bind the same port at the same time and the kernel load-balances new connections between them**. The `/healthz` pre-probe in `hubServe` only covers the "predecessor is already healthy" case; it does not cover:

1. **Simultaneous start** — the exact overlapping-run scenario this PR targets. Both processes fail the pre-probe (neither is up yet), both `shared: true` binds **succeed**, and both hubs serve one port: split roster/enrollments, last-writer-wins pid file, and each client randomly lands on either hub. Before this PR the loser exited 1 loudly ("something else holds the port").
2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor** — probe times out after 1 s under load while the old hub is alive → coexistence instead of a clear failure.
3. **Windows** — Dart maps `shared: true` to `SO_REUSEADDR` there, which binds over *any* existing holder (even a non-shared foreign server). The "foreign holder still exits 1" contract pinned in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` silently breaks on Windows (the CI matrix just doesn't run it there).

Note that the retry alone — without `shared: true` — already covers the stated vector: a dying predecessor's LISTEN socket closes and releases the port, and dart:io sets `SO_REUSEADDR` by default on POSIX, so TIME_WAIT does not block the re-bind. `shared: true` adds *only* the coexistence hazard.

This is also a **public API semantic change**: `LocalHub` is exported from `lib/io.dart`, and `start()` no longer throws `SocketException` on a taken port — that contract change is documented only in a test comment, not on `start()` itself.

Suggested hardening (any one):
- Drop `shared: true`; keep the healthz-aware retry (covers the dying-predecessor case with no split-brain window), or
- Keep it but add a post-bind re-probe: after a successful bind, re-probe `/healthz` for a short window and if *another* hub answers, `stop()` + take the idempotent "already running" exit, and
- Document the new "a second `start()` on a taken port shares it" contract in `start()`'s doc comment.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

This file has **no `@Timeout`** (every other PTY suite touched by this PR carries one, e.g. `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))`), `dart_test.yaml` sets no timeout override, and the CI invocation (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext`) passes no `--timeout`. So package:test's **default 30 s per-test timeout** applies.

Consequences for the new 60 s default:

- If the first frame arrives between 30 s and 60 s (the upper half of the stated 20-30 s cold-hook cost, plus margin), the **framework kills the test at 30 s** with a bare "Test timed out after 0:00:30.0" — the raised budget never helps, and the friendly `TimeoutException('pattern not found: … output:\n…')` dump at 60 s is unreachable, so failure diagnostics get *worse* than the old 20 s line.
- The 60 s timer only matters for pattern-not-found runs where the test would already have been torn down.

Fix: add a file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` (or per-test `timeout:`), matching the convention of the other suites in this PR, so the 60 s wait — and its diagnostic — can actually bind.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the fixed 50 ms close races its own premise — the retry path can go unexercised while the test stays green**

But if the serve prelude (process spawn + spec parse + the initial `/healthz` probe) takes >50 ms — common on a loaded runner, and this test exists *because* runners are loaded — the blocker is already gone when attempt 1 runs, attempt 1 binds directly, and the retry path is never driven. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

# pr-948: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled

## Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. The **#937 "stacked boards freeze" skip stays** — real product regression, deliberately untouched (per #938 policy).

## Local verification (sandbox: no PTY, plain dart + $TMPDIR PUB_CACHE)
- `dart test test/cli/fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test.dart test/cli/fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart test/hub/local_hub_test.dart test/hub/live_hub_test.dart` → **+40, all passed** (5 pre-existing env-conditional live-hub skips).
- `dart test test/integration/session_name_boot_perf_test.dart` → 3/3 green; `test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` → green (total=2433 ms).
- `dart analyze` clean on `bin/`, `lib/src/hub/`, and every touched test file.
- Zip determinism repro: mechanism + fix proven (above).

## Remaining (runner-side acceptance)
- The #943 acceptance runs themselves — two full PTY/CLI suites back-to-back plus the deliberate-overlap run — belong to the PTY runners (and CI is SM-owned). PTY-leg behavior here is inspection- + analyze-verified only; the harness/hub changes are exercised by every PTY suite the runners run next.
- The two full-suite runs + overlap simulation should be kicked by the SM on the next SM-scheduled ci.yml window for this PR.


---

## Round 2: rebased onto bd3b3c9 (#950) — catalog skip reconciliation
Rebased over #950 (Linux-only runtime skip for the catalog flake) and #945 (SM kicker). **The Linux-only skip is dropped, not kept:** the pin provably covers the failing assertion on both platforms — the sealed probe and the download path both re-run `zipOf`, whose every `ArchiveFile` carries `..lastModTime = _pinnedZipModTime` before `ZipEncoder().encode(archive)`, and pinned builds are byte-identical (throwaway repro: lazy wall-clock init proven; pinned encodes identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes — DOS packing is platform-independent integer math, no OS-dependent time source anywhere in the fixture). #950's runtime skip existed only because the unpinned encode could straddle the 2 s DOS tick; with the pin that premise is gone, so the Linux coverage #950 had to silence runs again. macOS keeps running it (as #950 already ensured). Scope checks after rebase: `dart analyze bin` clean; dispatch/ports/serve/local_hub +40 all passed. `flutter test` cannot run locally (read-only SDK cache — EPERM on engine.stamp); catalog runtime proof = next runner window.

+enum _BindOutcome {
+  /// The hub bound its port and may serve.

+  /// A hub came up on the port mid-retry — the idempotent no-op exit.
+  alreadyRunning,

+  refused,

+  /// The port was still held; another attempt follows.

+/// One bind attempt. On a [SocketException]: the last attempt is a
+/// hard [_BindOutcome.refused]; otherwise a live /healthz on the port
+/// means a hub came up mid-retry ([_BindOutcome.alreadyRunning]) and
+/// anything else asks for another round ([_BindOutcome.retry]).
+Future<(_BindOutcome, SocketException?)> _bindAttempt(
+  LocalHub hub,
+  int port,
+  bool lastAttempt,
+) async {
+  try {
+    await hub.start();
+    return (_BindOutcome.bound, null);
+  } on SocketException catch (error) {
+    if (lastAttempt) return (_BindOutcome.refused, error);
+    if (await hubHealthz(port)) return (_BindOutcome.alreadyRunning, error);
+    return (_BindOutcome.retry, error);

+/// Binds [hub] on [port], retrying with backoff (issue #943): an
+/// overlapping run's predecessor may still hold the port for a few

+/// the last [SocketException] for the message.
+Future<(_BindOutcome, SocketException?)> _bindWithRetry(
+  LocalHub hub,
+  int port,
+) async {
+  const attempts = 5;
+  SocketException? lastError;
+  for (var attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt++) {
+    final (outcome, error) =

+    if (outcome != _BindOutcome.retry) return (outcome, error);
+    lastError = error;
+    await Future<void>.delayed(_bindBackoff(attempt));
+  }
+  return (_BindOutcome.refused, lastError);

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

# them. Real-provider legs carry the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only
  # provider-smoke job; perf has its own #303 trajectory gate; browser-ext
  # its own workflow. `pty` marks child-agent-spawn tests whose second
  # process boot is unbounded under runner load (issue #553, red twice on
  # this leg) — they stay in nightly's pty-integration job.
  integration-mock:
    name: Integration tests (mock LLM)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: needs.changes.outputs.intmock == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Issue #943 (vector 3): warm the build hooks before the first test
      # process boots fa (same rationale as the pty-integration leg).
      - name: Prewarm build hooks + fa boot
        run: |
          dart bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null
          dart run bin/fah.dart --help > /dev/null

      - name: dart test test/integration (excluding llm, browser-ext, perf, pty)
        run: dart test test/integration --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty

  # Issue #675: the suite must be immune to a hostile ambient env — the
  # dmtools ai-teammate runner exports FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG /
  # FAH_PROVIDER, which used to decide test fate through the args resolver.
  # Run the non-integration suite under the same hostile env so any
  # ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:

Confirmed: `LocalHub.start()` silently coexists now. The split-brain scenario:

1. **Two simultaneous `fa hub serve` on the same port** (e.g., two overlapping CI runs, or a user double-start racing): both `/healthz` probes fail (neither is up yet), both bind `shared: true` → BOTH succeed → two independent hub processes serving the same port, kernel load-balancing WebSocket connections between them. Peers enrolled on hub A are invisible to hub B; `fa dap stop` SIGTERMs only the pid in the state file (the last writer). Before the PR: the loser exited 1 loudly. **This is a real regression in the idempotency guarantee.**

2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor**: healthz probe times out (1s) under load, bind shared:true succeeds → coexistence with a live-but-slow hub.

The healthz-then-bind window is inherent (TOCTOU), and `shared: true` converts that TOCTOU from "loud exit 1" to "silent split brain". The retry-with-backoff alone (keeping the bind exclusive) would deliver the same "dying predecessor picked up" benefit: a dying hub closes its listening socket, releasing the port; TIME_WAIT doesn't block a fresh listener with default SO_REUSEADDR semantics (Dart sets SO_REUSEADDR on non-shared binds on POSIX).

Hmm wait — actually, is that true? When a LISTENING socket is closed, are there lingering TIME_WAIT sockets that block a new bind? A listening socket with no connections: closing it leaves no TIME_WAIT (TIME_WAIT applies to connections in that state; a socket that only listened never established connections so no TIME_WAIT). {"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: `shared: true` turns a loud bind failure into a silent split-brain (and silently changes a public API contract)**

`LocalHub.start()` now binds with `shared: true`. On POSIX that sets `SO_REUSEPORT`, so **two fa hubs can bind the same port at the same time and the kernel load-balances new connections between them**. The `/healthz` pre-probe in `hubServe` only covers the "predecessor is already healthy" case; it does not cover:

1. **Simultaneous start** — the exact overlapping-run scenario this PR targets. Both processes fail the pre-probe (neither is up yet), both `shared: true` binds **succeed**, and both hubs serve one port: split roster/enrollments, last-writer-wins pid file, and each client randomly lands on either hub. Before this PR the loser exited 1 loudly ("something else holds the port").
2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor** — probe times out after 1 s under load while the old hub is alive → coexistence instead of a clear failure.
3. **Windows** — Dart maps `shared: true` to `SO_REUSEADDR` there, which binds over *any* existing holder (even a non-shared foreign server). The "foreign holder still exits 1" contract pinned in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` silently breaks on Windows (the CI matrix just doesn't run it there).

Note that the retry alone — without `shared: true` — already covers the stated vector: a dying predecessor's LISTEN socket closes and releases the port, and dart:io sets `SO_REUSEADDR` by default on POSIX, so TIME_WAIT does not block the re-bind. `shared: true` adds *only* the coexistence hazard.

This is also a **public API semantic change**: `LocalHub` is exported from `lib/io.dart`, and `start()` no longer throws `SocketException` on a taken port — that contract change is documented only in a test comment, not on `start()` itself.

Suggested hardening (any one):
- Drop `shared: true`; keep the healthz-aware retry (covers the dying-predecessor case with no split-brain window), or
- Keep it but add a post-bind re-probe: after a successful bind, re-probe `/healthz` for a short window and if *another* hub answers, `stop()` + take the idempotent "already running" exit, and
- Document the new "a second `start()` on a taken port shares it" contract in `start()`'s doc comment.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the 60 s `waitFor` default can never fire — the framework's 30 s per-test timeout binds first**

This file has **no `@Timeout`** (every other PTY suite touched by this PR carries one, e.g. `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))`), `dart_test.yaml` sets no timeout override, and the CI invocation (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext`) passes no `--timeout`. So package:test's **default 30 s per-test timeout** applies.

Consequences for the new 60 s default:

- If the first frame arrives between 30 s and 60 s (the upper half of the stated 20-30 s cold-hook cost, plus margin), the **framework kills the test at 30 s** with a bare "Test timed out after 0:00:30.0" — the raised budget never helps, and the friendly `TimeoutException('pattern not found: … output:\n…')` dump at 60 s is unreachable, so failure diagnostics get *worse* than the old 20 s line.
- The 60 s timer only matters for pattern-not-found runs where the test would already have been torn down.

Fix: add a file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` (or per-test `timeout:`), matching the convention of the other suites in this PR, so the 60 s wait — and its diagnostic — can actually bind.
"}

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: `shared: true` turns a loud bind failure into a silent split-brain (and silently changes a public API contract)**

`LocalHub.start()` now binds with `shared: true`. On POSIX that sets `SO_REUSEPORT`, so **two fa hubs can bind the same port at the same time and the kernel load-balances new connections between them**. The `/healthz` pre-probe in `hubServe` only covers the "predecessor is already healthy" case; it does not cover:

1. **Simultaneous start** — the exact overlapping-run scenario this PR targets. Both processes fail the pre-probe (neither is up yet), both `shared: true` binds **succeed**, and both hubs serve one port: split roster/enrollments, last-writer-wins pid file, and each client randomly lands on either hub. Before this PR the loser exited 1 loudly ("something else holds the port").
2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor** — probe times out after 1 s under load while the old hub is alive → coexistence instead of a clear failure.
3. **Windows** — Dart maps `shared: true` to `SO_REUSEADDR` there, which binds over *any* existing holder (even a non-shared foreign server). The "foreign holder still exits 1" contract pinned in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` silently breaks on Windows (the CI matrix just doesn't run it there).

Note that the retry alone — without `shared: true` — already covers the stated vector: a dying predecessor's LISTEN socket closes and releases the port, and dart:io sets `SO_REUSEADDR` by default on POSIX, so TIME_WAIT does not block the re-bind. `shared: true` adds *only* the coexistence hazard.

This is also a **public API semantic change**: `LocalHub` is exported from `lib/io.dart`, and `start()` no longer throws `SocketException` on a taken port — that contract change is documented only in a test comment, not on `start()` itself.

Suggested hardening (any one):
- Drop `shared: true`; keep the healthz-aware retry (covers the dying-predecessor case with no split-brain window), or
- Keep it but add a post-bind re-probe: after a successful bind, re-probe `/healthz` for a short window and if *another* hub answers, `stop()` + take the idempotent "already running" exit, and
- Document the new "a second `start()` on a taken port shares it" contract in `start()`'s doc comment.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

This file has **no `@Timeout`** (every other PTY suite touched by this PR carries one, e.g. `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))`), `dart_test.yaml` sets no timeout override, and the CI invocation (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext`) passes no `--timeout`. So package:test's **default 30 s per-test timeout** applies.

Consequences for the new 60 s default:

- If the first frame arrives between 30 s and 60 s (the upper half of the stated 20-30 s cold-hook cost, plus margin), the **framework kills the test at 30 s** with a bare "Test timed out after 0:00:30.0" — the raised budget never helps, and the friendly `TimeoutException('pattern not found: … output:\n…')` dump at 60 s is unreachable, so failure diagnostics get *worse* than the old 20 s line.
- The 60 s timer only matters for pattern-not-found runs where the test would already have been torn down.

Fix: add a file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` (or per-test `timeout:`), matching the convention of the other suites in this PR, so the 60 s wait — and its diagnostic — can actually bind.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the fixed 50 ms close races its own premise — the retry path can go unexercised while the test stays green**

But if the serve prelude (process spawn + spec parse + the initial `/healthz` probe) takes >50 ms — common on a loaded runner, and this test exists *because* runners are loaded — the blocker is already gone when attempt 1 runs, attempt 1 binds directly, and the retry path is never driven. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 948
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/948
- **Title**: Fix #943: infra tests fixed properly — tmp roots, hub port hygiene, prewarm, budgets; #938 skips re-enabled
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/943-infra-tests` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +339
- **Deletions**: -93
- **Created**: 2026-09-25T07:26:49Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-25T10:08:05Z

## PR Description

Fixes #943 (owner directive; diagnosis #936; re-enables the #938 skips in the same PR — items 1-6 all landed here).

## Delivered vs remaining, per item

**1. Unique per-run temp roots — DELIVERED, inspection-verified (PTY-leg runtime = runner-verified later).**
- `FaCliHarness._shortDefaultCwd` → `Directory.systemTemp.createTempSync('fa_pty_cwd_')` per spawn; the harness owns the dir and deletes it in `close()`/`hardKill()` **after** the CLI is dead, failure-safe (`on FileSystemException` swallow). `/tmp/fa_pty_cwd` is gone.
- `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.
- Foreign-attach kill at the harness layer: `FaCliHarness.spawn` pins `DAP_HUB_URL`/`DAP_LOCAL_HUB_URL` to a dead loopback port (override via `extraEnv`), so a boot can never dial — or auto-start against — an orphaned zero-config 8787 hub. This is the vector behind the contaminated composer-grid/picker frames.
- `wireHubTerminate` gains a `watchSignals` test seam (production wiring unchanged).
- Contract update pinned in `local_hub_test` ("binding a TAKEN port shares it…"); the foreign-holder exit-1 contract stays green in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test`.

**3. Build-hook prewarm + snapshot headroom — DELIVERED, workflow-verified by inspection (CI itself is SM-owned; never dispatched).**
- `ci.yml`: `pty-integration`, `pty-visual`, and `integration-mock` each warm the native-assets build hooks with one `dart bin/fah.dart --help` + `dart run bin/fah.dart --help` boot before the test phase (both invocation shapes the suites use).
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` wait default 20 s → 60 s.

**4. Perf budgets from measured clean runs + headroom — DELIVERED; the two in-process gates locally run.**
- `session_name_boot_perf` 2 s → **6 s** (AC3+AC4): local clean p95 is sub-second (2026-09-25, M4 Pro — all three tests finished inside the first wall second), CI-idle ceiling sat at the old 2 s line, concurrent-CI dilation 2-3×; still 6× under the ~36 s pre-fix regression class.
- `trajectory/perf_open_gate` totalMs 6000 → **9000**: CI idle sample 4737-5098 ms (four runs cited in-file), local clean 2433 ms (measured on this PR's branch); `buildMs <= 1000` DoD line unchanged.
- `pty_resume_equivalence` 45 s → **60 s** budget, tail wait 60 s → 90 s so the budget binds before the wait does. Inspection-derived only — needs a PTY host to measure.

**5. Hosted-parity flakes — ROOT-CAUSED, one fixed, one fixed-by-seam; mechanism locally proven.**
- `catalog_service_test`: **the zip-tick lead confirmed at byte level.** archive 4.3.0 `ArchiveFile.lastModTime` is a `late` field initializing to `DateTime.now()` at first access; the fixture sealed the sha from one `ZipEncoder` build and the `MockClient` rebuilt the zip for the download — a straddle of the 2 s DOS tick produced different bytes → sha mismatch. Fix: `lastModTime` pinned to a constant → every build byte-identical. Throwaway repro proved: lazy wall-clock init; same-second encodes identical (why it's rare); pinned builds identical; a ≥2 s pin delta provably changes the encoded bytes. *(Runtime proof under `flutter test` = runner-verified; flutter SDK is read-only here.)*
- `fah_hub_serve_dispatch_test` hostile-env leg: root cause = the "wired but not fired" test wired **real** SIGINT/SIGTERM watchers, so the hosted runner's orphan-cleanup pkill fired the graceful exit mid-test. Fixed by construction: new `watchSignals` seam injects no subscriptions (real-signal wiring stays covered by `test/hub/fah_hub_serve_test.dart`), test re-enabled. Also dropped the file's `freePort()` bind-close TOCTOU for port-0 hubs.

**6. #938 skips re-enabled — DELIVERED (12 sites), same PR per the issue's "one mechanical PR".**
All `@Skip`/`skip:` annotations referencing #936/#938 are gone: catalog_service, tui_prototype_snapshot (5 cases), scheduled_indicator, dap_cli_e2e, fa_cube, composer_tui_grid, picker_filter_rows, pty_resume_equivalence, session_name_boot_perf, perf_open_gate, dispatch hostile-env leg, job_board /tmp-racing case. - `job_board_stability_pty_test` fixture: `/tmp/fa_539_home` / `/tmp/fa_539_proj` → per-run `createTempSync` roots + failure-safe tearDown (the exact :98-99/:110-111 site from #936).
- `fa_cube_integration_test` tearDown failure-safe too (its "PathNotFound on cleanup" vector).
- Compile-clean (`dart analyze`); PTY runtime proof belongs to the runners (this sandbox denies PTY allocation machine-wide — `openpty` EPERM).

**2. Hub port hygiene — DELIVERED, runner-independent parts runner-verified locally.**
- `LocalHub.start()` binds `shared: true`; `hubServe` retries the bind with backoff (150 ms→1.2 s, 5 attempts), **re-probing `/healthz` between attempts**: a dying predecessor's port is picked up, a hub that comes up mid-retry takes the idempotent "already running" exit, and a genuinely foreign (non-shared) holder still exits 1 after the bounded window.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps

Actually SO_REUSEADDR on Windows: "allows a socket to forcibly bind to a port in use by another socket" — yes, second bind succeeds and behavior is undefined-ish (usually the second socket hijacks). This is a genuine platform-specific correctness concern → IMPORTANT (not blocking since CI platforms are POSIX and it matches Dart's documented cross-platform caveat... actually it IS a real behavior regression on Windows).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: `shared: true` turns a loud bind failure into a silent split-brain (and silently changes a public API contract)**

`LocalHub.start()` now binds with `shared: true`. On POSIX that sets `SO_REUSEPORT`, so **two fa hubs can bind the same port at the same time and the kernel load-balances new connections between them**. The `/healthz` pre-probe in `hubServe` only covers the "predecessor is already healthy" case; it does not cover:

1. **Simultaneous start** — the exact overlapping-run scenario this PR targets. Both processes fail the pre-probe (neither is up yet), both `shared: true` binds **succeed**, and both hubs serve one port: split roster/enrollments, last-writer-wins pid file, and each client randomly lands on either hub. Before this PR the loser exited 1 loudly ("something else holds the port").
2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor** — probe times out after 1 s under load while the old hub is alive → coexistence instead of a clear failure.
3. **Windows** — Dart maps `shared: true` to `SO_REUSEADDR` there, which binds over *any* existing holder (even a non-shared foreign server). The "foreign holder still exits 1" contract pinned in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` silently breaks on Windows (the CI matrix just doesn't run it there).

Note that the retry alone — without `shared: true` — already covers the stated vector: a dying predecessor's LISTEN socket closes and releases the port, and dart:io sets `SO_REUSEADDR` by default on POSIX, so TIME_WAIT does not block the re-bind. `shared: true` adds *only* the coexistence hazard.

This is also a **public API semantic change**: `LocalHub` is exported from `lib/io.dart`, and `start()` no longer throws `SocketException` on a taken port — that contract change is documented only in a test comment, not on `start()` itself.

Suggested hardening (any one):
- Drop `shared: true`; keep the healthz-aware retry (covers the dying-predecessor case with no split-brain window), or
- Keep it but add a post-bind re-probe: after a successful bind, re-probe `/healthz` for a short window and if *another* hub answers, `stop()` + take the idempotent "already running" exit, and
- Document the new "a second `start()` on a taken port shares it" contract in `start()`'s doc comment.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"🚨 **IMPORTANT: the 60 s `waitFor` default can never fire — the framework's 30 s per-test timeout binds first**

This file has **no `@Timeout`** (every other PTY suite touched by this PR carries one, e.g. `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))`), `dart_test.yaml` sets no timeout override, and the CI invocation (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext`) passes no `--timeout`. So package:test's **default 30 s per-test timeout** applies.

Consequences for the new 60 s default:

- If the first frame arrives between 30 s and 60 s (the upper half of the stated 20-30 s cold-hook cost, plus margin), the **framework kills the test at 30 s** with a bare "Test timed out after 0:00:30.0" — the raised budget never helps, and the friendly `TimeoutException('pattern not found: … output:\n…')` dump at 60 s is unreachable, so failure diagnostics get *worse* than the old 20 s line.
- The 60 s timer only matters for pattern-not-found runs where the test would already have been torn down.

Fix: add a file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` (or per-test `timeout:`), matching the convention of the other suites in this PR, so the 60 s wait — and its diagnostic — can actually bind.
"}

## Automated Code Review — COMMENT

**Summary**: Solid, well-diagnosed infra-test PR — the zip mod-time pin, per-run temp roots, and the `watchSignals` seam are correct and locally verified (36 hub tests green, `dart analyze` clean apart from one info lint). - 💡 SUGGESTION — info lint `prefer_initializing_formals` on the new `pty_harness.dart:45` field (repo pattern: `// ignore:` as in `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart`).

**Next Steps**:

2. Add `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` to `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart`.
3. Optional: make the retry-path test deterministic; silence the lint; fix the comment.
4. Note: discussion history shows validation CI red on earlier heads; runner-side PTY acceptance is explicitly still pending — expect the re-enabled skips to be exercised only there.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: `shared: true` turns a loud bind failure into a silent split-brain (and silently changes a public API contract)**

`LocalHub.start()` now binds with `shared: true`. On POSIX that sets `SO_REUSEPORT`, so **two fa hubs can bind the same port at the same time and the kernel load-balances new connections between them**. The `/healthz` pre-probe in `hubServe` only covers the "predecessor is already healthy" case; it does not cover:

1. **Simultaneous start** — the exact overlapping-run scenario this PR targets. Both processes fail the pre-probe (neither is up yet), both `shared: true` binds **succeed**, and both hubs serve one port: split roster/enrollments, last-writer-wins pid file, and each client randomly lands on either hub. Before this PR the loser exited 1 loudly ("something else holds the port").
2. **Wedged-but-listening predecessor** — probe times out after 1 s under load while the old hub is alive → coexistence instead of a clear failure.
3. **Windows** — Dart maps `shared: true` to `SO_REUSEADDR` there, which binds over *any* existing holder (even a non-shared foreign server). The "foreign holder still exits 1" contract pinned in `fah_hub_serve_ports_test.dart` silently breaks on Windows (the CI matrix just doesn't run it there).

Note that the retry alone — without `shared: true` — already covers the stated vector: a dying predecessor's LISTEN socket closes and releases the port, and dart:io sets `SO_REUSEADDR` by default on POSIX, so TIME_WAIT does not block the re-bind. `shared: true` adds *only* the coexistence hazard.

This is also a **public API semantic change**: `LocalHub` is exported from `lib/io.dart`, and `start()` no longer throws `SocketException` on a taken port — that contract change is documented only in a test comment, not on `start()` itself.

Suggested hardening (any one):
- Drop `shared: true`; keep the healthz-aware retry (covers the dying-predecessor case with no split-brain window), or
- Keep it but add a post-bind re-probe: after a successful bind, re-probe `/healthz` for a short window and if *another* hub answers, `stop()` + take the idempotent "already running" exit, and
- Document the new "a second `start()` on a taken port shares it" contract in `start()`'s doc comment.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

🚨 **IMPORTANT: the 60 s `waitFor` default can never fire — the framework's 30 s per-test timeout binds first**

This file has **no `@Timeout`** (every other PTY suite touched by this PR carries one, e.g. `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 10))`), `dart_test.yaml` sets no timeout override, and the CI invocation (`dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext`) passes no `--timeout`. So package:test's **default 30 s per-test timeout** applies.

Consequences for the new 60 s default:

- If the first frame arrives between 30 s and 60 s (the upper half of the stated 20-30 s cold-hook cost, plus margin), the **framework kills the test at 30 s** with a bare "Test timed out after 0:00:30.0" — the raised budget never helps, and the friendly `TimeoutException('pattern not found: … output:\n…')` dump at 60 s is unreachable, so failure diagnostics get *worse* than the old 20 s line.
- The 60 s timer only matters for pattern-not-found runs where the test would already have been torn down.

Fix: add a file-level `@Timeout(Duration(minutes: 2))` (or per-test `timeout:`), matching the convention of the other suites in this PR, so the 60 s wait — and its diagnostic — can actually bind.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-25):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the fixed 50 ms close races its own premise — the retry path can go unexercised while the test stays green**

The blocker closes at a fixed t=50 ms, "inside the first backoff window". But if the serve prelude (process spawn + spec parse + the initial `/healthz` probe) takes >50 ms — common on a loaded runner, and this test exists *because* runners are loaded — the blocker is already gone when attempt 1 runs, attempt 1 binds directly, and the retry path is never driven. The assertions (`code == 0`, `loopRan == 1`) pass either way, so the test silently degrades to a plain happy-path re-run.

Deterministic alternative: close the blocker after its **first accepted connection** — attempt 1's bind fails, its `hubHealthz` probe connects (and is destroyed) → that accept event orders the close strictly after the first failed bind, so attempt 2 always exercises the retry:
